answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a nadir as the anchor of the cost.
